name: Ngombe (Central African Republic)
world_status: statement found in a copy we already had

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog entry is retired/bookkeeping-only; only Monino comparative data and Ouzilleau 1911 vocabularies, no phonological description

new_statements.quote: Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345). [p. 345:] L'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles n'impose pas cette solution en proto-gbaya, mais l'hypothèse est envisageable à un niveau antérieur de l'évolution.
new_statements.translation: Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them presently shows any phenomenon of accent, of intensity or of length. The hypothesis will be raised again diachronically, when interpreting the sound correspondences (p. 345). [p. 345:] The absence of accent in the present-day languages does not impose this solution for Proto-Gbaya, but the hypothesis can be envisaged at an earlier stage of the evolution.
new_statements.citation: Moñino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative historique sur vingt-et-une langues d'Afrique centrale (SELAF 357; Langues et cultures africaines 20). Paris/Louvain: Peeters.
new_statements.locator: Part I ch. 16 'Récapitulation contrastive', p. 285, Remarque 2 (cross-reference to p. 345, Remarque)
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the page images we hold and Google Books publisher preview of Moñino 1995, Le proto-gbaya, SELAF 357) and read them visually, not just the scanned. p. 285 (running head RÉCAPITULATION CONTRASTIVE), Remarque 2, reads exactly: 'A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345).' p. 345 (CORRESPONDANCES PHONIQUES),…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bangando-Ngombe, like all 21 Gbaya languages in Moñino's survey, is a two-tone language (H/B, with floating grammatical tones per Boursier et al. 1984) with no accent: the author states that none of the present-day Gbaya languages has any accent, intensity (stress) or length phenomenon. On the same page bangando is singled out as having no relational morpheme and no morphological tone change.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the only qualification is diachronic (an accent is conceivable at a pre-Proto-Gbaya stage).
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level negative statement in the contrastive recapitulation of 21 first-hand phonological sketches (Bangando data collected by Moñino at Yokaduma from Cameroonian Bangando speakers, pp. 51-52). Strictly, 'les langues concernées' on p. 285 are those showing syllable-type-conditioned tone changes (area a); p. 345 generalises to 'les langues actuelles'. The language-specific chapter 15 'Bangando-ngombe' (pp. 254-268) could not be opened, so no Ngombe-specific sentence on accent was seen. CAR Ngombe itself was not surveyed by Moñino; he treats bàngàndò-ngómbé as one language (p. 16, p. 254).
new_statements.identity_note: ngom1265 / ISO nmj is a Glottolog bookkeeping (spurious) entry: the Ngombe of western CAR (Gamboula area, Mambéré-Kadéï) speak the same Gbaya language as the Bangando/Bangandu of SE Cameroon [bgf], Glottolog bang1347 'Ngombe-Bangandu' (Gbaya Meridional). Moñino 1995 describes them jointly as 'bangando-ngombe' from Cameroonian Bangando informants (Yokaduma); Boursier et al. 1984 describe Bangando of Salapoumbé-Moloundou (Cameroon); only Syssa & Pagbanda 2013 has first-hand CAR Ngombe data (wordlist, no prosody). Any catalog entry should be filed under bang1347, not as a separate language. Not to be confused with Bantu Ngombe [ngc] of DR Congo or the Bangombe Baka-Gundi clan.
